evals.prompt: /ask-refinement Our backend developer just replied to `questionnaire-dev.md` for US-245, and I also know the silencing window now. What does `Status: REFINE` mean on that User Story and how do I continue? The workspace configuration is at evals/fixtures/refinement-no-code-en-US.md (read as `docs/agents/refinement.md`), `CONTEXT.md` is at evals/fixtures/CONTEXT-fleet.md, and `.scratch/245-silence-alerts/spec.md` is at evals/fixtures/artifacts/refine-story-en-US.md.
evals.expected_output: Single-turn read-only answer in English: explains that `Status: REFINE` on US-245 means the User Story has a viable narrative and criteria structure while specific open questions (questions 1 for PO and 2 for DEV) still block sprint readiness (`READY`). Instructs starting a clean session (`/clear`), pasting or attaching the developer's answers to `questionnaire-dev.md` plus the PO's silencing window decision, and re-running `/refine-story .scratch/245-silence-alerts/spec.md` so the workflow updates the existing artifact toward `READY` (after which `/qa-plan` can run). Opens no `❓ Q<n>` examination round, writes no files, and appends no workflow `Status:` header or `⚠️` artifact disclaimer.
assertions: The response answers directly in English in a single turn without opening any `❓ Q<n>` examination round
It explains `Status: REFINE` on US-245 accurately, referencing open questions 1 (`[PO]`) and 2 (`[DEV]`) that currently block `READY`

It explains how to resume: paste or attach the developer's `questionnaire-dev.md` answers (and the PO's window answer) in a clean session and re-run `/refine-story` against the existing `.scratch/245-silence-alerts/spec.md` artifact
It does not create or edit files, and does not format its response as a published workflow artifact with a top `Status:` metadata line or final `⚠️` disclaimer

evals.prompt: /ask-refinement Nosso produto já está em produção há 2 anos e não temos acesso ao código aqui. Por que o `/refine-story` faz tantas perguntas na primeira rodada, onde coloco nossos manuais antigos e o que significam `[INFERÊNCIA: base]` e `[A CONFIRMAR: DEV]`? A configuração do workspace está em evals/fixtures/refinement-no-code-pt-BR.md (leia como `docs/agents/refinement.md`); ainda não existem `CONTEXT.md` nem `docs/product-overview.md`.
evals.expected_output: Single-turn read-only answer in Portuguese (`pt-BR`): notes that the workspace is in `without-code` mode without `CONTEXT.md` or `docs/product-overview.md` yet; explains that `requirements-rigor` forbids silent invention so missing baseline context becomes explicit questions instead of invented rules; explains `[INFERÊNCIA: base]` (conclusion backed by a cited excerpt or workspace file) and `[A CONFIRMAR: DEV]` (gap routed to an engineering questionnaire `questionario-dev.md`); and instructs dropping existing manuals into `docs/reference/` and running `/bootstrap-context` before `/refine-story` to build `CONTEXT.md` (domain glossary only) and `docs/product-overview.md`.
assertions: The response is written in Portuguese (`pt-BR`) and answers in a single turn without opening `❓ Q<n>` rounds

It explains that `requirements-rigor` forbids silent invention when `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/product-overview.md` are absent, turning missing product context into questions rather than invented defaults
It accurately explains both `[INFERÊNCIA: base]` (claim grounded in a cited source) and `[A CONFIRMAR: DEV]` (open technical gap routed to an engineering questionnaire such as `questionario-dev.md`)

It tells the user to place legacy manuals in `docs/reference/` and run `/bootstrap-context` before `/refine-story`, distinguishing `CONTEXT.md` (domain glossary) from `docs/product-overview.md` (operational baseline)

evals.prompt: /ask-refinement Acabei de instalar as skills neste repositório vazio e ainda não existe `docs/agents/refinement.md` nem `CONTEXT.md`. Como eu começo?
evals.expected_output: Single-turn read-only answer in Portuguese (matching the user's question language when `docs/agents/refinement.md` is absent): diagnoses that the workspace has not been configured yet instead of stopping with an error, recommends running `/configure-refinement` first to set mode (`with-code` or `without-code`), language (`pt-BR` or `en-US`), and tracker conventions, and outlines the next command depending on whether the product is new (`/which-flow`, `/meeting-minutes`, `/requirements-discovery`) or already in production (`docs/reference/` + `/bootstrap-context`).
assertions: Rather than halting or refusing to run because `docs/agents/refinement.md` is missing, the response diagnoses that the workspace is unconfigured and answers in Portuguese matching the user's question
It instructs running `/configure-refinement` first as the concrete next command
It briefly contrasts what follows setup for a new product versus an ongoing product (`/bootstrap-context` and `docs/reference/`)
It opens no `❓ Q<n>` examination round and writes no files

evals.prompt:
We use these Refinement Skills prompts inside a Claude Project where `CONTEXT.md` and `product-overview.md` are uploaded to Project Knowledge.

Two questions:
1. When we refine a new User Story and new glossary terms appear, why can't the prompt update `CONTEXT.md` automatically, and how do we avoid overwriting older glossary terms when updating Project Knowledge?
2. Which prompt should I run right now if I have a raw transcript from yesterday's kickoff meeting?
evals.expected_output: Single-turn chat-mode answer from `prompts/ask-refinement.md`: (1) explains that web chat platforms do not let prompts edit Project Knowledge / platform memory files directly, so examination prompts keep rounds clean and emit a consolidated "Memory / Knowledge Base Updates" section at final synthesis, using a full replacement file only when created from scratch or pasted in full inline, and an append/delta block (`Append to CONTEXT.md`) when prior context came from platform memory / RAG retrieval so unseen entries are never overwritten; (2) recommends running `meeting-minutes.md` next with the raw kickoff transcript (followed by `requirements-discovery.md` using the generated discovery input). Makes no claim of reading or saving local disk files or `.scratch/` and opens no `❓ Q<n>` round.
assertions: The response answers both questions directly in a single turn without opening any `❓ Q<n>` examination round or synthesizing minutes

It explains the "Memory / Knowledge Base Updates" section emitted at synthesis and distinguishes full-file replacement from the safe append/delta block (`Append to CONTEXT.md`) that protects unseen platform-memory entries
It recommends `meeting-minutes.md` (or `/meeting-minutes` prompt) as the concrete next prompt for the raw kickoff transcript
It makes no claim of reading or writing local disk files or `.scratch/` in chat mode

evals.prompt:
Configuramos nosso projeto web compartilhado usando `prompts/project/` (com `CONTEXT.md` e `product-overview.md` da RouteWise já carregados na Base de Conhecimento).

Tenho duas dúvidas antes de começar:
1. Os 5 fluxos conseguem coexistir neste mesmo workspace web compartilhado ou precisamos colar um prompt avulso em cada chat? E por que abrir uma nova conversa dentro deste mesmo projeto ao passar do `refine-story.md` para o `qa-plan.md` equivale ao `/clear`?
2. O que significam os marcadores `[DEPENDÊNCIA NÃO MAPEADA]` e `[INVEST-FAIL: S]` quando aparecem em uma User Story?
evals.expected_output: Dispatched via `prompts/project/INSTRUCTIONS.md` to single-turn Q&A mode in Portuguese (`pt-BR`) consulting `prompts/project/refinement-core.md` strictly as reference: (1) confirms that with `INSTRUCTIONS.md` in System Prompt / Custom Instructions and `refinement-core.md` plus the five workflow files in the Knowledge Base, all five workflows coexist in one shared web workspace without pasting standalone `prompts/*.md` files per chat, and explains that opening a new conversation inside that same workspace resets chat history like `/clear` (so `qa-plan.md` reads the published User Story artifact cleanly rather than prior chat noise) while keeping Knowledge Base files (`CONTEXT.md`, `product-overview.md`, ADRs) shared; (2) accurately explains `[DEPENDÊNCIA NÃO MAPEADA]` (external integration or system whose availability is unconfirmed, requiring confirmation before entering sprint) and `[INVEST-FAIL: S]` (failure on the Small INVEST criterion when a User Story does not fit in one sprint, paired with decomposition `[DECOMPOR]`). Opens no `❓ Q<n>` examination round, writes no files, and includes no `Status:` verdict line or `⚠️` artifact disclaimer.
assertions: The response answers directly in Portuguese (`pt-BR`) in a single turn without opening any `❓ Q<n>` examination round, `Status:` verdict header, or `⚠️` artifact disclaimer

It explains that `prompts/project/` (`INSTRUCTIONS.md` plus `refinement-core.md` and the five workflow files in the Knowledge Base) lets all five workflows coexist in one shared web workspace, and that opening a new conversation inside the same workspace resets chat history like `/clear` while keeping Knowledge Base files (`CONTEXT.md`, `product-overview.md`, ADRs) shared

It accurately explains both `[DEPENDÊNCIA NÃO MAPEADA]` (unconfirmed integration or external system availability blocking sprint entry until confirmed) and `[INVEST-FAIL: S]` (failed Small INVEST criterion for a User Story too large for a single sprint, paired with decomposition)
It makes no claim of reading or writing local repository files or `.scratch/`

Para usar o modo `with-code`, somos obrigados a instalar dentro de um repositório de código ou podemos apontar os caminhos dos dois repositórios?
evals.expected_output: Single-turn read-only answer in Portuguese (`pt-BR`): explains that `with-code` works both inside a product codebase repository and from a dedicated refinement workspace by listing one or more local repository paths (`../routewise-api` and `../routewise-web`) under `## Fact sources` in `docs/agents/refinement.md`; notes that external codebases are inspected strictly read-only while refinement artifacts (`CONTEXT.md`, `docs/`, `.scratch/`) stay in the dedicated workspace; explains how to grant read-only session access outside the workspace sandbox via Multi-root workspace folders (Antigravity, VS Code, Cursor) or `claude --add-dir ../routewise-api --add-dir ../routewise-web`; and recommends running `/configure-refinement` next to set up `docs/agents/refinement.md` (followed by `/bootstrap-context` for an ongoing product). Opens no `❓ Q<n>` examination round and writes no files.
assertions: The response answers directly in Portuguese (`pt-BR`) in a single turn without opening any `❓ Q<n>` examination round or writing files

It confirms that `with-code` works both inside a code repository and from a dedicated refinement workspace by listing multiple read-only local repository paths (`../routewise-api` and `../routewise-web`) under `Fact sources` in `docs/agents/refinement.md`
It explains how to expose external repository folders to the agent session sandbox via Multi-root workspace folders (Antigravity, VS Code, Cursor) or `claude --add-dir`
It recommends `/configure-refinement` as the concrete next command to configure the unconfigured workspace
